gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Panasonic's own figures under the current JIS C 8708:2019 test are about 600 cycles for eneloop AA and about 150 for eneloop pro AA. That test drains the cell fully before each recharge. The widely quoted 2,100 and 500 come from the old JIS 2013 test, which uses low current and never empties the cell, so they cannot be lined up against Tenergy's 1,200 or IKEA's 500, which name no test at all.
standout_why: I compared against the two cited pages and three of the top uncited results. Digital Camera World (cited) gives eneloop pro 'Recharge up to: 500 times' and names no test standard. The cited Which? sample tests only IKEA LADDA and Energizer and quotes no maker cycle figures. Which?'s buying guide (#8) says how Which? judges cycle life (80% and 60% of initial capacity) but does not explain the makers' figures. GeekChamp (#2) says 'up to 2,100 reuses under specified test conditions' and does not name the test. RottenWiFi (#5) mentions 'IEC-based procedures' only in general terms. None of them gives the 600 or 150 full-discharge figures, the 2019 JIS revision, or the fact that the 2,100 comes from a shallow test.
decides: It backs eneloop standard as the long-life pick: on Panasonic's own like-for-like full-discharge test it lasts about 4 times as many cycles as eneloop pro (600 vs 150). It weakens eneloop pro for camera flashes, because flash use drains cells fully, which is the case where the 150 figure applies, not the 500. It also means the page's 'Cycles (maker)' column cannot rank eneloop's 2,100 against Tenergy's 1,200 or LADDA's 500: those makers cite no test. The only independent full-discharge number I found is from Which?: LADDA 2450 'lost about a third after 200 cycles'. The column should footnote the test, or show eneloop as 600 / pro as 150 (JIS 2019).

findings.label: Cycle life, current JIS (full discharge before recharge)
findings.note: Panasonic's footnote ** says this is a life estimate under JIS C8708 2019 (7.5.1.4) test conditions. Panasonic describes it as large-current use, with the cell used up before recharging. The page lists the Japanese model BK-3MCD (AA min 2000 mAh). Panasonic says the battery's performance did not change, only the test, so the figure should carry over to the 2,100-cycle cells sold in the US. That carry-over is my inference, not a Panasonic statement.

findings.label: Cycle life, old JIS (shallow, low-current)
findings.note: Footnote *: JIS C8708 2013 (7.5.1.3). Panasonic describes the test as small-current use, recharged without using up the capacity. Panasonic: 'In March 2019 the JIS revision changed the cycle test conditions... the battery's performance itself has not changed.' This 2,100 is the figure on US packs and in ChatGPT's answer.

findings.label: Cycle life, current JIS vs old JIS
findings.value: about 150 cycles (JIS 2019) vs about 500 cycles (old JIS 2013)
findings.note: Chart text: 'エネループ プロ、単3形 min 2500 mAh … 現行JIS規格：約150回、旧JIS規格：約500回' (AA min 2500 mAh; current JIS about 150 cycles, old JIS about 500). Same footnotes as the standard model. Ratio to standard eneloop: 600/150 = 4.0× on the current test and 2100/500 = 4.2× on the old test.

findings.product: Panasonic eneloop AA / eneloop pro AA

findings.value: minimum ratings: eneloop AA min 2,000 mAh; eneloop pro AA min 2,500 mAh
findings.note: Panasonic states minimum values only. IKEA's 2,450 mAh and Tenergy's 2,800 mAh are not labelled min or typical, so the mAh figures are not on the same basis either.

findings.product: Panasonic eneloop AA / eneloop pro AA

findings.note: Footnote ※4: stored at room temperature (20 °C) after a full charge, with remaining capacity measured by the JIS C8708 2019 (7.3.2) discharge. The page's table shows eneloop at 70% after 10 years and pro at 85% after 1 year. On the same 1-year basis these are 90% and 85%.
